*Changes in 0.19:* brought onto `main`. The layout tables are built by `tools/cad/readme.py` from `metrics.json`. Hazard and requirement cross-references from the drafting branch are left out until the findings are mapped onto the records under `safety/` and `requirements/` (§4).

> **Concept mockups, not designs.** Every layout is built from solids placed by placeholder parameters. Dimensions, masses and every metric are properties of that placeholder geometry. They exist so the team can look at the same picture, compare alternatives side by side and see early where an option makes a hazard worse. They select nothing, and no rendering establishes feasibility. AI-drafted (independence I0), not reviewed.

![Concept line-up: open-frame bipeds with the UAV docked on the back (CL-01), on the shoulder (CL-02) and on a separate ground station (CL-03), the armoured pod (CL-04) and the reverse-jointed pod (CL-05), each with a 1.75 m person for scale](../../cad/renders/lineup.png)

## 1. What the layouts compare

Each layout (`CL-nn`) is one combination of architecture alternatives. Locomotion is **bipedal** (decided by the project lead on 2026-11-11, DQ-013). CL-01 to CL-03 share one open-frame biped, a centralized hydraulic actuation hypothesis (drawn as yellow cylinders) and a seated protected cockpit, and differ only in where the UAV docks. CL-04 is an armoured-pod restyle. CL-05 is the **reference layout** (chosen by the project lead, DQ-014): a tall pod with front and side windows, reverse-jointed legs and long claw arms, with its proportions taken from the lead's AI-generated Industrial Utility Walker. Neither CL-04 nor CL-05 reuses a source mesh or image; both are original parametric geometry, and CL-05 is authored in build123d code. Standing and remote-pilot stations and electromechanical actuation are not modelled yet.

What to look for in the review:

| Question | Where it shows |
|---|---|
| Can it stand without active balance? | Plan view: centre of gravity against the support polygon; static margin and tip angle |
| How far does the pilot drop on egress? | Side view: cockpit floor height |
| How close are docked rotors to the pilot? | Dock view: shortest rotor-to-pilot distance |
| How big is it next to a person? | Every view: the 1.75 m figure |

Metric definitions: *static margin* is the shortest horizontal distance from the centre of gravity to the edge of the support polygon (the convex hull of the ground contacts); *static tip angle* is the angle whose tangent is margin ÷ CG height; *placeholder mass* comes from solid volumes times the effective densities in [`params/common.yaml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/params/common.yaml). Values marked ⚠, or drawn in red on the images, are below 0.3 m static margin or 1.0 m rotor clearance, the provisional review flags. They are not requirements. Static margin is a standstill measure only: walking needs a dynamic stability analysis.

## 2. Reference layout CL-05

Rendered with Blender 5.3 (Cycles) by [`tools/cad/blender_render.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/blender_render.py) from exactly the meshes the metrics and drawing sheets use; only materials, daylight and camera are added. Concept renders for communication: placeholder geometry, not a design, and not AI-generated.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![CL-05 standing in olive-drab military livery, with a 1.75 m person for scale](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-hero-military.jpg) | ![CL-05 kneeling in military livery with the ladder deployed](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-kneel-military.jpg) |
| ![CL-05 from the rear in military livery: power pack, raised dock and roll bar](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-rear-military.jpg) | ![CL-05 emergency exit in military livery: hatch open, shoulder step and rope ladder](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-emergency-military.jpg) |

**Carrying a load** (placeholder load, mass TBD). Carrying while walking is allowed under conditions (decided by the project lead on 2026-11-12, DQ-015; SYS-019, HAZ-MAN-002): a secured load, the arms locked in a carry pose, and mass, centre-of-gravity, speed, step-height and slope limits that are all still TBD.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![CL-05 carrying a placeholder load clamped between its hands ahead of the pod, with a 1.75 m person for scale](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-carry.jpg) | ![CL-05 carrying a placeholder load in military livery](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-carry-military.jpg) |

**Walk cycle** (military livery; `cl05.py --walk 48`, then `blender_walk.py`): [![CL-05 walking in military livery with the arms stowed, side view tracking alongside, with a 1.75 m person standing still for scale](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-walk-military.gif)](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/renders/blender/CL-05-walk-military.mp4)

Every frame is the build123d model re-posed by the gait in [`params/CL-05.yaml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/params/CL-05.yaml) (`walk:`): stride 1.0 m, each foot planted for 60 % of the cycle and swung on a 0.22 m arc for the rest, with a small crouch and body bob. The knees are solved from hip and ankle positions, so they always bend backward exactly as in the CAD. The arms are stowed while walking: upper arm 45° down beside the hull and forearm folded nearly upright, which lifts the lowest claw from 0.85 m to 2.43 m and pulls the claw tips back from 1.77 m to 1.49 m ahead of the hips. This is concept kinematics for communication only: there is no dynamics, balance, actuator or load model behind it, and it says nothing about whether the walker can walk this way.

**Loaded walk** (military livery; `cl05.py --walk 48 --loaded`, then `blender_walk.py --loaded`): [![CL-05 walking in military livery with the placeholder load clamped between its hands, side view tracking alongside, with a 1.75 m person standing still for scale](../../cad/renders/blender/CL-05-walk-loaded-military.gif)](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/renders/blender/CL-05-walk-loaded-military.mp4)

The same gait with the arms locked in the carry pose and shorter, lower steps (`walk: loaded:` stride 0.70 m instead of 1.0 m, foot lift 0.16 m instead of 0.22 m): concept values standing in for the loaded speed and step-height limits of SYS-019, which are TBD. The load rides with the body's crouch and bob, keeps at least 0.89 m from the legs through the cycle and never drops below 1.42 m. As with the unloaded clip there is no dynamics, balance or load model behind it: it shows the pose and the motion, not that the walker can carry a load this way (HAZ-MAN-002, HAZ-WLK-002).

**AI concept art** made from these renders (Higgsfield, image-to-image) is kept apart in [`concept-art/`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/concept-art/README.md), each image labelled with its source render and where it departs from the CAD. It is for communication, never for dimensions.

### CL-05 findings

- **Reverse-jointed legs.** The knees sit behind the hips, the centre of gravity sits behind the hips, and a backward fall puts the knees first. Fall direction, the kneel and the stability limits need their own analysis for this leg geometry (HAZ-WLK-002).
- **Kneel for egress.** With the feet planted and the knees folded back, the hip drops from 2.34 m to 0.95 m and the cockpit floor from 2.41 m to about 1.0 m. A fold-down ladder under the front sill deploys in the kneel (four treads, largest rise 0.33 m), with grab handles for three points of contact. Standing, the ladder is stowed, so a failure that prevents kneeling also blocks normal egress. Lowering and rising create a crush zone under the pod and knees (HAZ-WLK-003, SYS-018; ingress and egress HAZ-PIL-001).
- **Emergency exit.** Both side windows are push-out hatches (clear opening 0.62 × 0.72 m) with internal release handles, so the pilot can leave standing and without power. The shoulder plate under each hatch is a step flush with the sill, and a fold-out davit carries a rope ladder clear of the walker. The sill is 3.2 m up: the descent is a fall-from-height hazard (HAZ-PIL-003, SYS-020). Whether the opening suits a pilot in protective equipment is TBD.
- **Stability.** Heel spurs reaching 0.68 m behind the ankle give a static margin of 0.38 m standing and 0.35 m kneeling, above the 0.30 m flag. Long heels add a trip risk on rough ground and a crush zone behind each foot (HAZ-WLK-002).
- **Rotor clearance.** The UAV dock is raised 0.45 m on struts so the docked rotors are 1.09 m from the pilot's head (over the 1 m flag; HAZ-DCK-001); they are then 0.29 m from the roll bar, which launch and recovery must clear (HAZ-INT-001). Taller struts are a longer lever for dock loads while walking.
- **Claws.** Hanging, the claws are inside the walking envelope, a strike and pinch zone. Stowed for walking they sit about 2.4 m up, still at head height beside a moving walker: stowage reduces the strike zone but does not remove it, and must be interlocked with walking (HAZ-MAN-001, SYS-017).
- **Carry pose.** The load is clamped between the hands 0.10 m ahead of the pod with its centre 1.80 m up, so its top stays under the pilot's sight line over the window sill (the nearest ground seen straight ahead stays 3.98 m). Load mass is TBD, so it is left out of the placeholder centre of gravity. At standstill, relative to placeholder mass, a load ahead of the pod first improves the margin, reaches the 0.30 m flag at about 2,580 kg and tips the standing walker forward at about 5,910 kg. These are not limits: walking adds swing and inertial loads, and the payload limits must come from the dynamic analysis (SYS-019, HAZ-MAN-002). Against the 0.12 m centre-of-mass offset cap (SYS-008, DQ-011) the combined centre of mass reaches 0.12 m ahead of the ankles at about 2,000 kg on placeholder mass and flat ground, also indicative only (HAZ-WLK-002). The load sits where the fold-down ladder lands, so it must be set down before kneeling for egress.

## 4. How the layouts are made

| Step | Tool | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Parameters | [`params/CL-nn.yaml`](Layout-Parameters.md), [`params/common.yaml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/params/common.yaml) | One file per layout; placeholders, metres |
| Reference layout geometry (CL-05) | [`tools/cad/b3d/cl05.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/b3d/cl05.py) in build123d 0.9 ([`environment.yml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/b3d/environment.yml)) | `build/cad-src/CL-05*/`: one STEP file per part class and `info.json`, per posture; `--walk N` writes walk-cycle frames |
| Geometry and metrics | [`tools/cad/build_concepts.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/build_concepts.py) under FreeCAD 1.1 | `build/cad/CL-nn/`: `.FCStd`, `.step`, STL per part class; [`metrics.json`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/metrics.json) (committed) |
| Drawing sheets | [`tools/cad/drawings.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/drawings.py) (FreeCAD TechDraw hidden-line projection) | [`drawings/`](Drawing-Sheets.md) SVG and [`concept-layouts.pdf`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/drawings/concept-layouts.pdf) (committed): 420 × 297 mm 1:50, third-angle side, plan and front views; the revision in the title block is read from this page's header |
| Photoreal renders and walk clip (CL-05) | [`tools/cad/blender_render.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/blender_render.py), [`tools/cad/blender_walk.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/blender_walk.py); Blender 5.3 `bpy` module, Cycles | [`renders/blender/`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/tree/main/cad/renders/blender) (committed; not run in CI) |
| Review images | [`tools/cad/render.cjs`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/render.cjs) and [`viewer.html`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/viewer.html) (three.js in headless Chromium) | [`renders/`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/tree/main/cad/renders) (committed) |
| This page | [`tools/cad/readme.py`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/readme.py) | §3, from `metrics.json` and the layout parameters |
| Front-page banner | `tools/readme/build_readme.py` | `docs/readme/banner.svg`, composed from the CL-05 renders |

Run everything with `tools/cad/make.sh` (it needs FreeCAD 1.1, see [`tools/cad/environment.yml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/tools/cad/environment.yml), build123d, and Node with Playwright). CI ([`.github/workflows/cad.yaml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/.github/workflows/cad.yaml)) rebuilds the geometry on every change to `cad/` or `tools/cad/`, fails if `metrics.json` or a drawing sheet is out of date, and attaches the STEP, FCStd and STL files and the drawing PDF to the run. CAD files are not committed; they are reproducible from the parameters.

## 5. Next

1. Review the layouts with the systems, safety and human-factors leads.
2. Replace effective densities with a mass budget once a parts breakdown exists.
3. Decide the licence for hardware design files before the first design-level CAD.

## Purpose

This folder holds the concept layouts of SUS-M1 (SUS-CAD-001): parameters, the metrics and drawing sheets built from them, renders and concept art. They let the team compare alternatives on one picture and see early where an option makes a hazard worse; they select nothing. The sections below are generated from `metrics.json` and the records; the review above is hand-written.

## Where the findings went

![Figure 2 · Where the CL-05 findings went](../../cad/figures/fig-2-findings.svg)

| Finding | Records |
|---|---|
| Reverse-jointed legs | HAZ-WLK-002 |
| Kneel for egress | HAZ-WLK-003, SYS-018, HAZ-PIL-001 |
| Emergency exit | HAZ-PIL-003, SYS-020 |
| Stability | HAZ-WLK-002 |
| Rotor clearance | HAZ-DCK-001, HAZ-INT-001 |
| Claws | HAZ-MAN-001, SYS-017 |
| Carry pose | SYS-019, HAZ-MAN-002, SYS-008, DQ-011, HAZ-WLK-002 |

Records that cite the CAD: 12 hazards (HAZ-DCK-001, HAZ-GSE-001, HAZ-INT-001, HAZ-MAN-001, HAZ-MAN-002, HAZ-PIL-001, HAZ-PIL-003, HAZ-PIL-004, HAZ-PIL-005, HAZ-PIL-006, HAZ-WLK-002, HAZ-WLK-003), 5 requirements (SYS-016, SYS-017, SYS-018, SYS-019, SYS-020) and 6 decisions (DQ-013, DQ-014, DQ-015, DQ-022, DQ-023, DQ-024).

## Block diagram

![Figure 3 · Block diagram](../../cad/figures/fig-3-block-diagram.svg)

## Boundary diagram

![Figure 4 · Boundary diagram](../../cad/figures/fig-4-boundary-diagram.svg)

| # | From | To | Crossing / interaction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Decision register | Layout parameters | biped, reference layout, carry (DQ-013 to DQ-015) |
| 2 | Layout parameters | CAD build | placeholder dimensions |
| 3 | CAD build | Metrics, drawings and renders | metrics.json, sheets, images |
| 4 | Concept layouts | Hazard and requirement records | findings cited by HAZ and SYS records |
| 5 | Concept layouts | Front page README | banner from the CL-05 renders |
| 6 | Metrics, drawings and renders | AI concept art | source renders (concept-art/) |
| 7 | CI | CAD build | rebuild; fail on stale metrics or sheets |
| 8 | Named human review | Concept layouts | layout review (not done) |

**Explicitly excluded:** design-level CAD, manufacturing data and any claim of feasibility; CAD files themselves (rebuilt from the parameters, not committed).

## SysML model

[`ConceptLayouts.sysml`](https://github.com/jherrodthomas/Project-Susanoo/blob/main/cad/ConceptLayouts.sysml) is generated from `metrics.json` and validated with the project model by the OMG pilot in CI.
